title: The tube on the floor
objective: Recognize tension pneumothorax and a dislodged or disconnected chest tube as emergencies, and know the immediate response

sources.cite: Progressive care nursing certification exam handbook and test plan: Respiratory (14% of the exam)
sources.note: Relayed from the PCCN course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/pccn.ts), which read the handbook 2026-11-14, not re-read: Respiratory is 14% of the exam. Scope only.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN). Nursing Advanced Skills, 6.4 Troubleshooting Problems and Complications. WisTech Open, 2023
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. If the chest tube is accidentally removed from the patient, 'cover the chest tube insertion site with a sterile occlusive dressing and tape it on three sides', the open side letting air escape to reduce the risk of tension pneumothorax; have a colleague 'immediately notify the provider' while you stay with the patient; call the rapid response team for respiratory distress or a sudden change in vital signs. For a disconnection from the drainage system: 'Call for assistance in replacing the drainage system and notifying the provider', momentarily clamp near the chest wall or place the distal end in sterile water.
Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.

brief.situation: 10:05 on a progressive care unit. Mr. Osei, 58, has a right chest tube for a pneumothorax. The physical therapist calls you to the hallway: as he turned, the tube pulled out. It is lying on the floor and the insertion site is hissing.
handover: The tube was still bubbling with an air leak this morning. SpO2 95% on 2 L by nasal cannula before the walk.

Unit policy: cover a pulled-out chest tube site with a sterile occlusive dressing taped on three sides, stay with the patient, have a colleague notify the provider at once, and call rapid response for respiratory distress.
Never reinsert a tube. The provider is on the unit.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and act as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

The provider notified within 5 minutes of the tube coming out (unit policy).
The site covered with a three-sided occlusive dressing within 5 minutes (unit policy).
A focused assessment or question: about 1 min.
About 10 minutes for the provider to arrive with a new tube tray and the patient back in bed; a routine plan about 10 minutes.

why.question: Mr. Osei's chest tube is out and the site is hissing. What do you do, and why that dressing?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: A pulled-out chest tube with an ongoing air leak leaves an open chest wound; air can enter and the pneumothorax will grow; a fully sealed dressing could trap air and cause tension.
parts.modelAnswer: The tube is out and he still had an air leak, so air is moving through the hole and the lung will collapse further. Sealing it on all four sides could trap air and cause tension.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Sterile occlusive dressing taped on three sides; stay with him; a colleague gets the provider now; back to bed on oxygen; watch for tension signs; never reinsert.
parts.modelAnswer: Cover it with a sterile occlusive dressing taped on three sides, stay with him, have a colleague get the provider now, get him back to bed on oxygen, and watch for tension. I won't push the tube back.

noProgress.rationale: An open chest tube site still without a new tube an hour on is harm here.

scoring.modelReasoning: A pulled-out chest tube with an air leak leaves an open chest. The site is covered at once with a sterile occlusive dressing taped on three sides so air can escape but not enter; a fully sealed dressing could cause tension. You stay with him while a colleague gets the provider, get him back to bed on oxygen, and watch for tension. The tube is never pushed back in.

discQ.ask: While the provider works: if a chest tube disconnects from the drainage system instead, what is the first step?

choices.label: Momentarily clamp near the chest wall or put the end in sterile water, and call for help

discQ.explain: For a disconnection: call for assistance, momentarily clamp near the insertion site, or place the distal end in sterile water.
